status.en: 12 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 37% fewer than the week before, most of them in Baghdad, Kirkuk and Erbil.
status.nb: 12 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 37 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Baghdad, Kirkuk og Erbil.

summary.en: US troops have completed their withdrawal, leaving Iraq to confront new security and governance challenges while Gulf states rank higher in disaster resilience than Iraq. Baghdad and Tehran are deepening security cooperation and have activated joint committees, even as Iran’s envoy warned that border security is a red line and Iranian forces attacked the Komala Kurdish opposition group. Iraqi authorities are pursuing legal action against media incitement supporting pro-Iran armed groups, arresting a lawyer who brandished a gun in court and urging prosecutions, while the YBŞ is negotiating integration into state security institutions. Nineveh continues heritage reconstruction and the Jordanian king has invited the Iraqi president for regional de-escalation talks. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: US-troppene har fullført tilbaketrekningen, og etterlater Irak med nye sikkerhets‑ og styringsutfordringer mens gulfstatene rangerer høyere i katastrofe-resiliens enn Irak. Bagdad og Teheran utdyper sikkerhetssamarbeidet og har aktivert felles komiteer, selv om Irans utsending advarte om at grensesikkerhet er en rød linje og iranske styrker angrep opposisjonsgruppen Komala. Iraks myndigheter forfølger rettslige skritt mot medieoppfordringer som støtter pro-iranske væpnede grupper, arresterte en advokat som trakk en pistol i retten og oppfordrer til påtaler, mens YBŞ forhandler om integrering i statlige sikkerhetsinstitusjoner. Nineve fortsetter gjenoppbygging av kulturarv og den jordanske kongen har invitert Iraks president til regionale de-eskaleringssamtaler. Konflikten registrerte 396 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Iraqi conflict
background.extract: The Iraqi conflict is a series of violent events that began with the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq and deposition of Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein, followed by a series of conflicts including the protracted Iraq War (2003–2011), the Iraqi insurgency (2011–2013), the War in Iraq (2013–2017), and most recently, the small-scale Islamic State insurgency in 4 provinces located in Northern Iraq since 2017.
